# The NOTICE and TRADEMARKS files name the holder and the year, not placeholders
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #366, sha256:7bd4eeabbcb221ee33b22c2d9476d9734b52720490d7e7dff2586bf7cc66d9ae). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Draft
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** story
- **Repository:** avowry (NOTICE, TRADEMARKS.md)
- **Source:** product-owner answers to the nine owner items on docs/release/pre-publication-checks.md, inbox entry of 2026-11-08 (card 186). Ranked before the v0.1 publish card.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Dana, I want the NOTICE and TRADEMARKS files to name the holder and the year, so that I can see who owns the Avowry name before I adopt it.
- **Consumer value:** Dana reads a real holder line in both files when she checks the licence and trademark terms of the first preview.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Scenario: [O][S] holder and year are filled
     Given the owner's answer: holder "Programming Made EZ", year 2026 (an assumption the owner can correct), the same holder on the trademark line
     When Dana opens NOTICE and TRADEMARKS.md
     Then both name "Programming Made EZ", NOTICE carries 2026, and no square-bracket placeholder remains in either file
  2. Scenario: [Z][E] nothing else changes
     Given the LICENSE file and the other tracked files
     When the holder is filled
     Then LICENSE is unchanged, and the page records the year as an assumption the owner can correct
  3. Scenario: [I] a guard
     Given the placeholder text that card 186's test looks for
     When the files are filled
     Then a test fails if a square-bracket placeholder returns to either file
- **Not in this card:** The trademark search itself (card for the owner-items page update); LICENSE text.
- **Size:** S
